metaDescription: Six countertop dishwashers compared on place settings, tank or faucet hookup, drying and programs for apartments, dorms and small kitchens.
expertTake: The COMFEE' 6 place setting Energy Star model is the pick for most small households because it holds a real two to three person load and connects to the faucet. The COMFEE' tank model is the pick when you have no sink hookup. Skip a countertop dishwasher if you cook with large pots and pans daily, because they will not fit. Check plate diameter and pot height against the interior before you order.
introParagraphs: A countertop dishwasher is a compact wash chamber with a small pump, spray arms and a heater, sized to sit on a counter. It suits apartments, dorms, RVs and small kitchens where a built-in unit is not possible. Most also run on standard household power, so no special wiring is needed.

They save water against handwashing, but capacity is limited and loading takes thought. The comparison below separates real capacity from marketing, and tank models from faucet-fed ones. Water use is low, roughly two to three gallons a load, but time per cycle is long, often an hour or more.

products.name: COMFEE' 6 Place Setting Energy Star Countertop Dishwasher
products.description:
This is the largest machine in the roundup, sized for two or three people, with six place settings and eight cycles including Heavy, Normal, Baby-Care, ECO, Glass and Speed. At roughly 17 by 22 by 20 inches it takes real counter space, which is the price of the capacity.

It connects directly to the faucet with a suitable adapter, so it fills and drains through the sink instead of using a tank. That removes the refill chore of tank models but requires a compatible faucet. Against the 5-liter tank units, it can run longer loads without interruption.

The Energy Star rating signals efficient water and power use. Measure the cabinet clearance above and the counter depth before buying, scrape plates and load carefully. For a small household that wants one real daily load, it is the best fit. In year three, the parts that need attention are the door seal and the filter, both of which collect grease from daily loads. Against the BLACK+DECKER it offers one more cycle and a larger chamber, while the BLACK+DECKER offers a brand with a longer parts record. Plan to scrape plates, load bowls on the sides and leave tall pots to hand washing.
products.bestFor: Two or three people who want a true daily load.
pros: Six place settings, the largest here
Eight cycles including Heavy and Baby-Care

products.name: COMFEE' Countertop Dishwasher with 1.32-Gallon Tank 6 Programs
products.description:
A 1.32-gallon tank lets you fill the washer by hand and run it anywhere there is an outlet. This suits renters and RVs where faucet hookup is awkward. Six programs include Normal, Rapid, Hygiene, Fruit, Glass and Air Refresh.

The Hygiene cycle heats water to 158 degrees Fahrenheit, which helps with greasy dishes and baby items. Air Refresh circulates air to keep dishes and the chamber fresh, which is better than passive drying alone. Compared with the six-place COMFEE', it is smaller and ties you to the tank size.

Fill the tank with clean water, load carefully and let the door vent after a cycle. It is the better choice when you cannot connect to a faucet. Because the tank holds only about five liters, a single cycle uses all of it, so refilling is part of every run. Against the HAVA softener model it lacks scale control, which matters if your tap water is hard. Empty the tank after the cycle to avoid stale water smells.
products.bestFor: Renters and RV owners without a faucet hookup.
pros: No hookup needed with a built-in tank
Hygiene cycle heats water to 158 F

products.name: HAVA TDJR09 Countertop Dishwasher with Water Softener
products.description:
The standout feature is an integrated water softener. In hard-water areas, scale builds on spray arms and leaves spots on glass, so a softener extends the machine life and improves results. That is rare at this size.

It also adds an optimized ECO mode for lower water and energy use and a redesigned adjustable basket that improves loading. Against the standard HAVA with a 5-liter tank, this version targets results and efficiency rather than extra programs.

Use softener salt as the manual directs, clean the filter regularly and check the spray arm ports. It is the pick for hard-water households. Hard-water scale is the silent killer of small spray arms, whose ports are tiny, so a softener protects the very part that fails first. Against the COMFEE tank unit it trades the hygiene heat for scale protection, so choose based on your water.
products.bestFor: Hard-water kitchens that fight spotting and scale.
cons: Costs more than basic tank models

products.name: BLACK+DECKER BCD6W Energy Star Countertop Dishwasher
products.description:
BLACK+DECKER is the only long-established appliance brand in the group, which matters for parts and support. It offers seven wash cycles, an LED display and a Quick Connect assembly for the faucet.

The Energy Star rating signals efficient use, and the LED display makes cycle selection easy. Against the COMFEE' six-place unit, it has fewer cycles but a more recognized brand. Quick Connect makes hooking to the faucet less fiddly than a threaded adapter.

Wash dishes after scraping, load carefully and keep the filter clean. It suits buyers who value brand recognition. Quick Connect also makes it easy to remove the hose between uses so the counter stays clear. Against the six-place COMFEE it offers a recognized name rather than extra capacity, and warranty claims tend to be simpler with an established brand.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want an established brand and Energy Star efficiency.
cons: Needs a faucet; no tank mode

products.name: FOHERE Countertop Dishwasher with Delay Start 5+1 Programs
products.description:
At 16.2 by 15.5 by 17.8 inches, this is the smallest machine in the roundup, with a 1 to 6 hour delay start that lets you run cycles at off-peak times. Five programs plus one extra cover the usual loads.

The compact footprint suits tiny kitchens and dorms. Dual spray arms provide 360-degree coverage in a small chamber. Against the COMFEE' six-place unit, capacity is lower, so it fits one to two people.

No installation is needed beyond filling the tank or connecting a hose. Load plates upright and keep large pots out of the plan. It is the smallest option. Delay start is useful if your power plan charges more in the evening, or if you want the machine to run while you are out. Against the EUHOMY it is smaller and has fewer programs, so it fits a single-person kitchen better.

products.name: EUHOMY Countertop Dishwasher 8 Programs 5L Tank 40 dB
products.description:
EUHOMY offers eight programs and a 5-liter tank in a quiet 40 dB design, sized for 30-plus items. Plates up to 10.25 inches fit, along with bowls, cups, utensils and baby items.

The tank or hose option adds flexibility, and the 40 dB rating suits open apartments. Against the six-place COMFEE', capacity is smaller, but the program count is higher and the unit quieter.

Use the hose for long loads to avoid refilling. It suits apartment dwellers who value quiet. The 40 dB rating, if it holds in daily use, makes it the pick for studio apartments where the dishwasher runs near the bed. Against the FOHERE it has more programs and a bigger tank, but also a bigger body, so measure first.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Most countertop units hold four to six place settings, and the real number is lower than marketing. The COMFEE' lists 6 place settings, most tank units about 4, and the FOHERE is smaller. Large pots and pans often do not fit, so match capacity to your daily dishes, not weekend entertaining. A realistic test is whether your plates, bowls and one cooking pan fit together in a single load.

A built-in tank, about 5 liters on the HAVA, EUHOMY and COMFEE' tank unit, needs no plumbing but requires manual refilling. Faucet-fed units like the BLACK+DECKER and the 6-place COMFEE' fill and drain through the sink. Sprayer-style faucets can complicate the adapter. A tank also lets you place the unit away from the sink, which helps in narrow kitchens.

Passive drying relies on residual heat and a vented door and is weak on plastics. Hot-air or Air Refresh modes, as on the COMFEE' tank unit and EUHOMY, perform better. If you dislike towel-drying, prioritize active drying. Open the door slightly after the final rinse to let steam escape and speed up drying.

Normal, Eco, Rapid, Glass and a hygiene or baby-care cycle cover most needs. The COMFEE' hygiene cycle heats water to 158 degrees. More programs help only if you use them. Delay start, offered on the FOHERE, lets you run at night.

Hard water leaves scale and spots. The HAVA TDJR09 includes a softener, which is rare. Clean the filter regularly, since a clogged filter is the usual cause of poor results. Use rinse aid if your water leaves a film on glasses.

Units measure roughly 17 by 17 by 18 inches, while the 6-place COMFEE' is larger. They give off steam when finishing, so leave clearance. Measure the counter and the cabinet above. Do not open the door fully right after a hot cycle, as the steam can damage nearby cabinets.

specDecoder.meaning: A standard set of plate, bowl, cup and utensils. Real loads vary.
specDecoder.watchFor: The 6 place COMFEE' is rated for two to three people; others hold about four. Always check the interior height for dinner plates.

specDecoder.meaning: Built-in water volume, usually about 5 liters or 1.32 gallons.
specDecoder.watchFor: Tank models need refilling for each load. A hose option avoids this for longer loads.

specDecoder.meaning: A high-temperature wash for baby items and greasy dishes.
specDecoder.watchFor: The COMFEE' tank unit heats to 158 degrees Fahrenheit.

specDecoder.meaning: A noise rating at the unit.
specDecoder.watchFor: EUHOMY lists 40 dB; others do not state. Noise matters most in open-plan apartments.

specDecoder.meaning: A certification for efficient use of water and power.
specDecoder.watchFor: The BLACK+DECKER and 6-place COMFEE' carry it.

howWeEvaluated.title: Capacity and footprint
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared place settings and dimensions, from the FOHERE's compact 16.2 inch width to the COMFEE' six-place unit's larger body. Interior height and plate diameter limits, such as the EUHOMY 10.25 inch plate limit, were treated as part of capacity.

howWeEvaluated.title: Water supply
howWeEvaluated.description: We separated tank, faucet and dual-supply models, noting refill and compatibility trade-offs. Dual-supply models scored higher because they work in more kitchens.

howWeEvaluated.title: Drying and programs
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked for hot-air drying, hygiene cycles and delay start. Passive drying was treated as the baseline and active drying as a real advantage.

howWeEvaluated.title: Water quality
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked for softeners and filter design, since scale affects long-term results.

howWeEvaluated.title: Value and support
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed price tier and brand support, with BLACK+DECKER the established name, based on the spec sheet and owner feedback patterns.

cards.label: Tank (COMFEE' tank, EUHOMY, FOHERE)
cards.text: No plumbing and total placement freedom. You refill by hand and loads are limited by the tank.

cards.label: Faucet (BLACK+DECKER, COMFEE' 6 Place)
cards.text: Runs full loads without refilling. Needs a compatible faucet and sits near the sink.

howToChoose.note: Choose a tank if you rent or cannot reach a faucet. Choose faucet for daily loads.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: No installation, a tank or quick connect, and a footprint that fits your counter. Check the faucet type. Ask your landlord whether faucet adapters are allowed.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The COMFEE' tank model and FOHERE need no hookup, and the EUHOMY gives both options.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You have hard water or a daily full load: the HAVA TDJR09 or COMFEE' 6 Place.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You wash a few dishes and do not mind refilling: the COMFEE' tank or FOHERE.

maintenance.why: A clogged filter is the usual cause of poor results. Rinse it under running water and brush off stuck bits.
Food residue builds up and causes odors. Leave the door ajar after the final cycle of the day.
Hot water clears grease and scale from the chamber. An empty hot cycle with a cleaner sold for dishwashers works well.
Hard-water scale blocks ports. A soft brush clears them.

faq.a: They can be surprisingly effective for their size, but expectations should be realistic. Scrape plates and load carefully. Pre-rinsing is rarely needed, but food chunks should be scraped off. Glasses and flatware come out best, while baked-on pans do not.
Yes, roughly 2 to 3 gallons per load, well below handwashing. Cycle times are longer than a full-size machine, so run it overnight if possible. That makes it cheap to run daily.
Not for tank models. Faucet models need an adapter. A sprayer-style kitchen faucet often needs a different adapter, so check the faucet type first.
No. Use dishwasher detergent only, since hand soap creates suds. Tablets, powder and gel differ, so follow the manual.
Often not. Large pots and pans need hand washing. A cutting board or sheet pan will not fit either.
Quiet units are rated about 40 dB. Others are louder. Place a mat underneath to reduce vibration on hard counters.
